planner: US (State Dept Policy Planning Staff: Nitze, after talk with Brig. Gen. Loper, Army atomic energy)
source_doc: FRUS 1950 vol. VII Korea, doc. 745: Memorandum by the Director of the Policy Planning Staff (Nitze), 4 Nov 1950; https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1950v07/d745
quote: If the bomb should be used for strategic purposes through attacks on such Manchurian cities as Mukden, Fushun, Anshan, Harbin and Dairen, this action would result in the destruction of many civilians
notes: Examples of strategic atomic targets in Manchuria named in a memo that argues against such use (it "would almost certainly bring the Soviet Union into the war"); a policy discussion, not a target list. selected left blank: no decision recorded. Tactical use, by contrast, would be "against troop concentrations and artillery support positions" (p.1041), unnamed.

quote: a heavy blow could be dealt against the Communist economy by the destruction (by A-bombs if need be) of not only the Yalu River Dam but the other power installations in North Korea.
notes: Suggestion "on the eve or morrow of any later graver turn in the situation". The dam straddles the Korea-China border (modern name is an identification, not in the source). The companion row (other power installations) is a class without names.
